text:
maria: kicked off a cross-GPU attention kernel sweep — A100 / H100 / L40S. seq lens [256,512,1024,2048], batch sizes [1,4,8,16]. comparing flashed variants, paged-attn, fused-paged, and our hybrid selector.
liam: nice. which workload? gen vs chat (kv heavy)?
maria: gen synthetic (random tokens) + chat-like KV warmup to exercise spill/evict. prefetched KV on some runs to see behavior.
kevin: FYI added --kv-cache-prefetch=on/off toggles. command used:
```
./bench --model=gpt-like --gpu=A100,H100,L40S --seqs=256,512,1024,2048 --batches=1,4,8,16 --kernels=flash,paged,fused_paged,hybrid --kv-prefetch=true --runs=5
```
liam: any regressions?
maria: overall fused_paged wins at low seqs but H100 shows a weird latency spike at seq=2048, batch=8 for fused_paged. A100 and L40S fine.
zara: spike as in p99 or median?
maria: p50 ~ stable, p99 jumps 2.4x only on H100 fused_paged. throughput drops ~30%.
perf-bot: Automated profile uploaded: https://perf.redwood/reports/2367004444 (contains nvprof and trace).
kevin: looks like KV spill thrash — kernel selector picks fused_paged expecting contiguous KV but H100's L2 eviction pattern + our prefetch backend causes extra memcpy.
liam: can we repro with a minimal case? run single-stream seq=2048 batch=8, attach CUPTI trace.
maria: reproed locally. attaching short log snippet:
```
[H100][fused_paged] seq=2048 batch=8 tokens/sec=18k p99=112ms kernel_time=95ms kv_evictions=96 memcpy_ms=15
[H100][hybrid]    seq=2048 batch=8 tokens/sec=25k p99=48ms  kernel_time=42ms kv_evictions=4  memcpy_ms=2
```
zara: wow, memcpy dominates. selector threshold probably misclassifying long-seq patterns. we assume fused_paged reduces memcpy but here it's causing more because of extra kv spills.
kevin: hypothesis: our fused_paged launch path uses a larger workspace allocation that triggers H100 driver to fall back to a different mempool leading to non-coalesced copies. also see more kernel retries in the trace.
liam: plan: 1) roll a small tweak to selector: prefer hybrid for seq >= 1536 on H100; 2) add a runtime guard to detect memcpy_ms > 5ms and fallback; 3) schedule a fuller perf run with and without kv-prefetch.
maria: created PR draft with selector tweak:
```
if gpu == H100 and seq >= 1536 and batch >= 4: choose=hybrid
```
kevin: for (2) runtime guard: add a microtimer after kernel launch and if memcpy exceeds threshold, annotate and reroute next requests to hybrid for 30s. cheap and can auto-mitigate.
zara: we should also instrument kv cache hit/miss heatmaps per prefix length. that will help us refine thresholds.
maria: agree. I'll run the additional sweep (kv-prefetch on/off) overnight and post summarized heatmaps.
perf-bot: nightly job queued: job_id=perf-2367004444-regen. expected finish ~8h.
liam: great. after we validate, let's schedule a canary to Dedicated for a small % of traffic. add an opt-in flag so enterprise customers can control.
maria: noted. I will post results tomorrow and link to PR.
